title: Tie a necktie on a collar form
instruction: Tie the necktie on the collar form and leave it ready to wear.
context: Tying a necktie is a familiar dressing skill and a useful example of assistance for someone with limited hand movement.
setup: An adult 1.45 m woven polyester necktie with interlining and pointed ends, 70 mm wide end and 35 mm narrow end, nominal effective thickness 1.2 mm and mass 37.55 g. Pale and gold opposite-edge markings identify its front face: pale left and gold right with the wide tip down. A rigid plastic 110 mm-diameter, 100 mm-high neck form is centred at (0.400, 0, 1.250) m. A 162 mm-diameter, 5 mm-thick lower collar rim is centred at (0.400, 0, 1.2225) m. Fifteen rigid collar-flap pieces, each 3 × 15 × 60 mm, stand at z=1.250 m on a 79 mm-radius arc around the neck: angles −70° to +70° in 10° steps from +X, 3 mm dimension radial and 15 mm tangent. The front is open. A 210 × 25 × 25 mm rear arm is centred at (0.495, 0, 1.190) m; a 25 × 25 × 455 mm rear post at (0.590, 0, 0.975) m; and a 180 × 160 × 12 mm base at (0.590, 0, 0.7535) m on the YAM table at z=0.7475 m. A 3 mm dark centre mark is at (0.3449, 0, 1.250) m. Start with the tie untied and uncrossed around the collar, both ends accessible in front and the wide tip resting on the table. The shared five-second gravity settling uses the recorded untied reset shape, without any attachment. Length is measured downward from the neck form’s lower edge at z=1.200 m.
scoring: 0.5 for a genuine necktie knot retained after both hands release for 5 seconds. Increase this to 1.0 if the knot is centred within 20 mm horizontally, the neckband gap is at most 15 mm, the wide face is outward without a half-twist, the narrow end is behind it with its tip at least 10 mm higher, and the wide tip hangs 350–440 mm below the collar’s lower edge. No retained knot gives zero. Fabric damage, visible material passage, undisclosed support or artificial tightening gives zero.
run_limit: 3,600 control steps (180 seconds at 20 Hz), including the final 5-second released hold.
reset_notes: Restore the same untied, uncrossed drape shown in the setup image. The simulator loads the recorded naturally settled shape against the flat rest mesh, then settles for 5 seconds with ordinary ready-position actions. Both policies use this reset and the disclosed static-contact model.
fidelity: Native surface FEM models flexible cloth, gravity, stretch, bending and self-contact; tearing is not modelled. Contact-gated constraints approximate finger grip with 9 mm minimum joint clearance for compliant pads. Closing seats the enclosed patch; opening releases it. A 10 mm rear-collar contact approximates static friction. Slip forces are uncalibrated. The rest of the ribbon is free, without a target knot or automatic tightening. Both policies use the same model.
scores: Not evaluated. No demo or Dream score exists.
